newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends sharply up on good sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends sharply up on good sentiment.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended sharply up in active trading on Tuesday on expectations of further rises in the short term, traders said.
The most active February 1997 contract ended at 20,920 yuan ($2,520) per tonne, rising 330 yuan. It opened at an intra-day low of 20,660 and hit a high of 20,950.
December rose 270 to 20,470, January 300 to 20,800, March 310 to 20,960, April 340 to 20,960, May 370 to 20,970 and June 430 to 20,980.
Combined volume rose sharply to 110,720 tonnes from 56,540.
Copper opened higher and rose for most of the session.
Traders said overnight gains on the London Metal Exchange encouraged long position holders in Shanghai and that they expect copper to rise further in the next few days.
"Speculative buying from retail investors who followed institutional buyers pushed prices sharply up because they believed the technical rebound will continue for the next few days," one trader said.
"All contracts met strong resistance at the 21,000 yuan level, which indicated investors were afraid of large amouts of hedge selling at high levels," a second trader said.
"Falls in open interest with the rises of prices also indicated the wary attitude of most investors," he added.
Analysts expect Shanghai copper to follow the LME's trend in the next few days in the absence of domestic market-moving news.
Aluminium ended down. December fell 50 to 13,550 yuan per tonne, January did not trade and February fell 50 to 13,950.
Combined volume fell to 250 tonnes from 330.
